sourceFinding: The 2026–2027 pathway totals 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC courses in each of Years 1 and 2, 30 EC open study, three selected 6 EC subjects from seven, and a 12 EC thesis. The retained electives are Econometrics III, Machine Learning for Econometrics and Data Science, and Fair, Transparent and Interpretable Machine Learning; they are choices, not universal requirements. There is no formal graduation route. Teaching is English, with Dutch tutorial/expression/exam-answer options in Years 1–2. BSA requires 42 first-year EC, a pass in Calculus/Analysis I OR Analysis II/Mathematical Reasoning AND a pass in Introduction to Data Science OR Statistics. The English diagnostic or refresher gates Data Analysis I. Zero-credit BRIDGE requires attendance at five of six plenaries. Data Science Practical requires a final DSA mark or a Period-1 Econometrics I/Numerical Methods partial mark of at least5.5. Thesis entry requires120EC including minor and at least two passes from Econometrics II, Multivariate Statistics and Data Science Methods. The thesis is individual quantitative research with a paper and poster/presentation, assessed by supervisor and second reader; topics appear in Period4. The current July2027 diploma deadline concerns current final-year students, not the future Fall2026 entrant’s Year3. The minor normally requires90EC; open study has at most6EC level100, at least12EC level300 and no compulsory-course overlap. Prior board approval applies except stated faculty/university/Education-minor exemptions; the Economics university minor is prohibited for EDS. Course manuals may require attendance. Honours is additional and excluded.

all29ProfileContributions.ACCPPDE101: Mandatory first-year personal, academic and collaborative development; not quantitative thesis training.
all29ProfileContributions.BENBUSI112: Accounting and financial-statement/annual-report analysis supports interpreting firm data; not asset pricing, portfolios or capital budgeting.
all29ProfileContributions.BENBUSI211: Examines AI effects on competitiveness, innovation, labor, growth and corporate governance/fairness across business functions; supports critical organisational use of analytics, not technical ML.
all29ProfileContributions.BENECON111: Introduces microeconomic markets/consumer and firm behavior plus macroeconomic output, inflation and unemployment, providing economic interpretation for data analysis.
all29ProfileContributions.BENECON211: Develops macroeconomic dynamics, policy, growth, crises and trade; supplies economic interpretation for inflation and business-cycle questions, not econometric time-series estimation.
all29ProfileContributions.BENECON212: Analyzes consumer choice under uncertainty, preferences, imperfect competition and market efficiency; provides substantive demand/firm theory for quantitative applications.
all29ProfileContributions.BENECON312: Teaches OLS, GLS and IV, inference and Monte Carlo simulations in Stata with an empirical paper; directly implements applied estimation and prediction, not Econometrics II/III.
all29ProfileContributions.BENECON314: Uses biases, heuristics, framing and experiments to explain economic choices; complements the interpretation of economic data rather than specialist forecasting.
all29ProfileContributions.BENENTR211: Consumer psychology, trust, brand strategy and marketing plans supply the substantive consumer-engagement domain for the secondary analytics concept.
all29ProfileContributions.BENENTR311: Plans and executes market research, collecting and analyzing customer evidence and reporting results; no guaranteed causal advertising-effect estimator.
all29ProfileContributions.BENENTR312: Studies global business institutions, cross-border governance, responsibility and trade; a specific complement for business decisions and governance, not a data-science method.
all29ProfileContributions.BENGATE101: Team venture development includes customer/market validation and business-model testing, connecting quantitative inquiry to evidenced consumer/business decisions.
all29ProfileContributions.BENGATE102: Introductory research design, operationalisation, experiments, surveys, sampling and inference with a group project; not full multivariate or mathematical-statistics training.
all29ProfileContributions.DISARIN111: Philosophical and psychological AI ethics addresses fairness, bias, privacy and responsibility; it does not teach formal differential privacy or model-agnostic interpretability algorithms.
all29ProfileContributions.DISARIN211: AI planning under uncertainty and resource constraints is a specific computational-decision complement; not econometric or supervised-learning estimation.
all29ProfileContributions.DISARIN212: Discrete mathematics, logic and structures support algorithm construction and mathematical reasoning; not a substitute for Analysis II.
all29ProfileContributions.DISARIN311: Search, constraint satisfaction and numerical/convex optimisation projects support computational problem solving; not stochastic econometrics.
all29ProfileContributions.DISARIN312: Implements reinforcement-learning algorithms and neural-network agents learning by trial and error; extends computational learning beyond supervised modeling.
all29ProfileContributions.DISCOMP212: Relational database theory, SQL, normalisation, authorization and queries directly support structured data management.
all29ProfileContributions.DISCOMP311: Algorithm design, data structures and experimental performance analysis with laboratory projects directly implement efficient computational methods.
all29ProfileContributions.DISDATA111: Data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and a research project support practical empirical analysis; unlike VU’s identically named probability course.
all29ProfileContributions.DISDATA211: Regression/classification, resampling, shrinkage, trees, support vector machines and clustering implement statistical learning with real-data applications.
all29ProfileContributions.DISDATA311: Builds and trains neural networks in Python/TensorFlow, then computer-vision/text models; specialised empirical deep learning rather than generalisation-risk proofs.
all29ProfileContributions.DISGATE101: Python programming, data constructs, debugging and object-oriented problem solving provide the computational foundation.
all29ProfileContributions.DISGATE102: Differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations support quantitative methods; does not establish the full proof-based Analysis I/II sequence.
all29ProfileContributions.DISMATH211: Linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, transformations and eigenvalues support multivariate quantitative reasoning.
all29ProfileContributions.DISMATH213: Root finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation/integration and ODE algorithms develop accuracy/stability-aware numerical computation.
all29ProfileContributions.DISMATH312: Linear time-invariant signals, convolution and Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms contribute systems mathematics; not state-space econometrics or economic time-series forecasting.
all29ProfileContributions.DISMATH314: Probability, distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation provide mathematical statistics foundations for later modelling.

comparability: Mathematical/probability/programming/database/algorithm/numerical/ML and OLS-GLS-IV estimation provide substantive EDS methods. This is more than programme coherence. Econometrics and mathematical-learning depth gaps remain. Consumer/advertising interest supports a real market-research and consumer/business application with five different courses37.5EC each. Responsible ML already covered and lacks a distinct privacy/interpretability sequence, so stop at two.
